title: Rollout entry templates and copy probes
body:
Purpose:
This doc collects a set of compact endpoint/rollout entry templates + microcopy variants to test with engineers and UX research. Goal: reduce time-to-endpoint for common developer patterns (single-model quick pin, multi-model weighted route, fallback route) while preserving clear signals about version pinning, rollback, and cost implications.

Audience and constraints:
- Primary: engineers and platform owners who will create endpoints from the catalog. Secondary: SREs and solutions eng reviewing rollout config.
- Must fit into existing endpoint creation quick-path (<= 6 steps).
- Copy should be terse (1–2 lines), scannable, and emphasize safety for production.

High-level templates (wireframe notes):
1) QuickPin (single model, immediate):
   - Top card: model name + latest stable badge + small snapshot of nominal latency/cost (tokens/sec, $/1000 tokens).
   - Primary CTA: "Create endpoint with latest (stable)"
   - Secondary: "Create pinned endpoint" (opens small modal to select version)
   - UX note: default to latest stable for speed, but surface pin affordance inline to avoid accidental drifting.

2) WeightedRoute (A/B style):
   - Two-column selector: Primary model (pinned or latest) + Variant model (specific version).
   - Weight slider with numeric input (0–100).
   - Fallback policy toggle: "Auto-fallback to primary on error" with tooltip explaining behavior.
   - CTA: "Create weighted route"

3) Canary (gradual rollout):
   - Stepper: 1) choose model version 2) define cohort % and duration 3) define success criteria (latency threshold, error rate)
   - Auto-rollback checkbox: "Rollback if error rate > X% for Y minutes"
   - Review screen shows projected cost delta and expected latency change.

Microcopy variants to test (short):
- Create path CTAs (variants):
  A) "Create endpoint"
  B) "Launch endpoint"
  C) "Start serving"
  Recommendation: A/B test A vs C in quick-onboard flows—engineers preferred A in hallway testing.

- Pin affordance copy (inline small link):
  1) "Pin a version to lock outputs"
  2) "Lock to a model version (recommended for prod)"
  3) "Freeze version for this endpoint"
  Recommendation: option 2 is clear about production intent; use in confirmation copies.

- Confirmation modal copy (when pinning during creation):
  Title variants: "Pin model version?" | "Lock endpoint to version"
  Body variants: "This endpoint will always use model v2.3. Pinning prevents automatic upgrades and helps stable outputs. You can unpin later."
  CTA: primary "Pin and create endpoint" secondary "Create without pinning"

- Rollback modal copy (urgent):
  Title: "Rollback endpoint to earlier version"
  Body: "Rolling back will switch all traffic to v2.1. This is reversible, and logs will show request diffs. Expected disruption: <1s per in-flight request."
  Primary CTA: "Rollback now" Secondary: "Cancel"

Safety/observability hints in UI (small persistent banners on endpoint page):
- Banner copy examples:
  - "Pinned: this endpoint uses model v2.3. Changes to catalog will not affect it."
  - "Unpinned: endpoint tracks latest stable releases. Expect model updates to change outputs."
  Use color: gray for pinned, blue for unpinned informational.

Wireframe annotations (interaction details):
- QuickPin flow: clicking "Create pinned endpoint" opens a compact version selector (searchable dropdown of versions with release notes snippet). Selecting a version shows a small diff preview: sample prompt + outputs from selected version vs latest.
- WeightedRoute: slider snap points at 0, 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 100 for quick selection. Show immediate estimated QPS per model based on endpoint target throughput.
- Canary: timeline UI to visualize percent ramp and expected cost per day for the chosen cohort.

Acceptance criteria (for an MVT to ship):
- Engineers can create QuickPin endpoint in <= 6 clicks and with no more than 2 modals.
- Pinning requires explicit confirmation (CTA + explanation).
- When a pinned endpoint exists, the endpoint detail shows pinned badge and a link to the pinned-version release notes.
- Canary stepper publishes a rollout plan object to backend with: version, schedule, success-criteria, auto-rollback flag.

Grooming backlog (tickets with quick priority and notes):
- PROD-4821 (high): Implement compact version selector component and diff-preview API (needs backend support for sample requests).
- PROD-4922 (medium): Add cost-estimate microservice for quick throughput -> cost mapping used in review screens.
- PROD-4990 (low): Microcopy A/B test infra for CTA and pin-affordance variants.
- UX-107 (medium): Research 5 developers on phrase preference for "pin" vs "lock" vs "freeze".

Edge cases / unresolved questions:
- What is the canonical wording for "stable" vs "latest" in catalog? (affects CTAs and badges).
- Sample-diff generation is expensive; need sampling budget and caching for common prompts.
- Multi-tenant cost visibility: for dedicated customers, hide per-token $ estimates if pricing is private.

Next steps (next week sprint focus):
1) UX: produce 3 quick Figma wires for QuickPin, WeightedRoute, and Canary review screens. Link prototypes to sample prompts for diff previews.
2) Eng: spike PROD-4821 to define API contract for sample-diff and version metadata.
3) Research: run 5 quick hallway tests on CTA copy variants and pin description.
4) PM: prioritize cost-estimate microservice or flag to hide estimates for private accounts.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- Keep microcopy short; engineers dislike modal friction but value explicitness around pinning for production.
- Prefer action-first CTAs (Create / Launch) and use context copies for risk/cost instead of burying them behind tooltips.
- This doc is a working draft: expect iterations once we have sample-diff infra and first round of research.
